thread:
kevin: ran a 15m long-context run against master with the 3B model and KV cache tracing on. seeing steady memory creep (+~12% heap) and a rise in free-block count — looks like fragmentation, not leaks. attaching a few quick extracts.
perf-bot: profile summary uploaded: https://perf.internal/runs/3759991111 (kv_free_count=13412, frag_ratio=0.18, avg_free_block=128B) :white_check_mark:
mira: can you paste the block-size histogram? curious if tiny blocks dominate.
kevin: sure — quick sample from heap dump (block_size:count)
```
64: 7420
128: 3120
256: 1020
512: 280
1024: 72
>1024: 40
```
kevin: most free space is in the 64B and 128B buckets. many adjacent holes but allocator isn't coalescing them frequently.
sam: chunking strategy seems to favour small allocations for KV entries from short contexts. two ideas: bump the min slab to 128 or add a deferred coalesce pass when consecutive free blocks > N.
luca: also consider a background compaction that targets regions with high hole density rather than global scans. schedule low-prio cycles at <5% CPU to avoid latency spikes.
mira: tradeoffs: increasing min block wastes space for short-lived entries, but reduces fragmentation. background compaction risks token throughput jitter. do we have microbench numbers?
kevin: ran a microbench: background compactor merging up to 8 neighbors per cycle adds ~0.8-1.2% extra CPU and 0.6% token latency p99 in worst-case under synthetic noise. steady-state overhead closer to 0.3%.
sam: alternative hybrid: keep small-block fast-path + small arena per-thread, and when arena free fraction > threshold push its blocks to global compactor to consolidate. that avoids touching hot paths on alloc/free.
luca: can we detect long-context sessions and switch allocation profile per-request? e.g., pin large KV entries to big-block slab so long runs don't fragment small arenas.
mira: would need routing at request start; could be done by checking prompt length and expected context. maybe heuristic switch and mark the session for compaction on end.
kevin: i'm going to run two canaries: (A) increase min-block to 128 and run 1h workload; (B) enable background compactor with conservative parameters. will report metrics: frag_ratio, mem_growth_per_hour, p50/p95/p99 latency, cpu overhead.
sam: also add hist of coalesces per-second and number of merges per compaction cycle. that'll help tune.
luca: i'll prototype a compaction pager that merges only when hole_density > 0.25 and contiguous_free_bytes > 8KB. if perf looks OK i'll push a canary flag.
mira: sounds good. if canary (B) keeps latency within SLO and reduces mem growth we can iterate thresholds. thanks for the quick triage. :thumbsup:
